A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TMPC research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are available and readable, supporting comparison despite some internally inconsistent implementation descriptions.

before.justification: v3 reports original translation, long-form response, and MBPP experiments, together with robustness and runtime results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and adds threshold and principle ablations, fixed-boundary comparisons, and additional TPO results.

M1.justification: Sections 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same TMPC procedure. However, v3 H.3 describes storing successful system prompts, whereas v4 H.3.3 describes conditioning on buffered programs. v3 already mentions code conditioning elsewhere, and v4 H.3.2 still says system prompts are stored. These contradictions prevent distinguishing an actual procedure change from revised documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions use WMT’24 literary translation from Chinese into English, German, and Russian, the long-response HH-RLHF subset, and MBPP. The added comparisons and examples remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 5 adds evaluated Tower-7B sentence-by-sentence translation and fixed-boundary LLaMA-3.1 rewriting comparators. Best-of-20 disappears from the runtime comparison, although it remains in the response-quality comparison. The original main benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v4 adds four-iteration TPO evaluation alongside the existing two-iteration HH-RLHF setting, fixed-boundary translation controls, threshold/principle ablation settings, and throughput reporting. H.3.1 changes the reported MBPP rollout count from two to three per iteration; this establishes a reported budget revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 tests buffer/segment sizes, reward-model quality/noise, and iteration counts. v4 substantially broadens mechanism analysis with threshold sensitivity, approximate separate ablations of hindsight selection and subgoal conditioning, and fixed-boundary translation controls (Table 2 and Appendix E.2). Existing sensitivity and iteration analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing reward-noise perturbation setting is unchanged.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial result sets for threshold/principle ablations and fixed-boundary translation, plus four-iteration TPO reward of 4.39 and latency of 148 seconds. It adds throughput values and removes Best-of-20’s 28-second runtime entry. Table 1 and GPT-4 pairwise outcomes are unchanged; MBPP remains reported at 61% despite the revised rollout-budget description.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, trajectory objective, MPC/MPPI mathematics, and buffer/aggregation equations (1–5) are retained. Added explanations of the receding-horizon interpretation introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The first introduction contribution shifts the novelty claim from formulating alignment as sequential decision making to introducing a previously unexplored trajectory-optimization framework. The abstract and conclusion retain the same principal TMPC and three-task effectiveness claims.

C2.justification: v4 replaces blanket test-time translation superiority wording with best-or-second-best performance, consistent with Table 1’s Russian results. It adds explanations of threshold and principle-ablation effects and attributes Tower-7B’s Russian advantage to backbone capability. Appendix B’s general limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds task-specific buffer examples, revises the program-synthesis prompt, documents spaCy preprocessing for the new baseline, and discloses two A6000 GPUs for four-iteration TPO. It adds a project-page address while retaining the future code-release statement. Most training hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 discusses subgoal planning through Ren et al. (2019), Logeswaran et al. (2022), and Wang et al. (2025a), distinguishing TMPC’s frozen-model hindsight planning from earlier approaches. PPO references are also added. TreeBoN and TPO publication updates refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: Appendix H substantially expands the exposition with three worked subgoal walkthroughs, reverses the translation/response subsection order, and rewrites the program-synthesis discussion. The main text adds a related-work subsection, MPC explanations, expanded analysis, and acknowledgments. This is a substantial explanatory revision despite retaining the overall paper outline.

P2.justification: The results presentation is substantially reorganized: v3 Figure 5’s sensitivity panels become part of v4 Table 2, its iteration panel becomes standalone Figure 5, and the runtime chart becomes Table 6. v4 also adds Table 5, expands Figure 3 with another TPO bar, and redraws parts of the conceptual diagrams.

improvement.justification: The added principle ablations and fixed-boundary controls strengthen evidence for TMPC’s mechanisms, while four-iteration TPO results extend the previously memory-limited comparison. These provide a limited overall quality gain. Benefits are tempered by removing Best-of-20’s favorable 28-second runtime comparison and by an incomplete printed Python example and unreconciled implementation descriptions in Appendix H.
